categories.main_business_segments: Alleanza Holdings operates primarily in two business segments: home center retail (DIY, household goods, gardening, etc.) and pet specialty retail. The group manages several chains including Daiyu Eight, Time, Home Center Valor, and Amigo, with additional activities in agricultural product sales, imports/wholesale, and home renovation services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages efficient retail operations, private brand (PB) product development, and advanced logistics. It is actively implementing digital transformation (DX) initiatives such as AI-driven automated ordering, inventory optimization, and data analytics for marketing and operations. The group also focuses on supply chain integration and multi-format store development.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Alleanza Holdings serves general consumers, targeting households and pet owners in regional communities. Its main markets are the home improvement, daily goods, and pet care sectors, catering to both DIY enthusiasts and everyday shoppers seeking convenience and value.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in Japan, with a strong presence in the Tohoku, Chubu, and Chugoku regions, as well as the Kanto and Kansai areas. All stores and business activities are domestic, with no significant overseas operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Alleanza Holdings is positioned downstream in the supply chain as a retailer, directly selling products to end consumers through its network of home centers and pet stores. It also engages in some midstream activities through its import/wholesale subsidiary.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding private brand products, accelerating digital transformation (DX), optimizing logistics, and enhancing productivity. The group is also focused on sustainability (SDGs), diversity in human resources, and developing new store formats and e-commerce channels. M&A is used to broaden business domains and sales channels. There is no significant in-house R&D; innovation is mainly in business processes and retail operations.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through direct product sales at its retail stores and online channels. Additional income comes from services such as pet grooming, training, and home renovation. There are also minor revenues from wholesale and agricultural product sales.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other major Japanese home center chains (e.g., Cainz, Komeri, DCM) and pet specialty retailers. Alleanza Holdings is a leading regional player with a multi-brand, multi-format strategy, aiming to be the top pet retailer in Japan and a dominant home center operator in its core regions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending February 2025, consolidated sales were 153.3 billion yen, with operating profit of 3.5 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent shareholders of 2.1 billion yen. The company has a stable but modest growth profile, with recent years showing slight revenue increases but declining profits due to competitive and cost pressures. The group employs approximately 1,879 regular employees (plus 3,745 part-time/temporary staff).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Alleanza Holdings emphasizes customer satisfaction, regional community contribution, and convenience through a wide product assortment and competitive pricing. Its differentiation lies in the integration of home center and pet business formats, strong private brand development, and a focus on digital transformation and operational efficiency. The company also highlights its commitment to sustainability and local infrastructure support.
